title: Fragile Vials Across Stair Landing
description: Move a padded case of emergency medication 1.8 m across the level stairwell landing to the medical attendant. Stay inside the marked route behind the stair barrier, travelling forward at 0.045 m/s before sliding left 0.24 m over 12 seconds to the handoff mark. Staff load and unload the case; the robot never enters a stair flight.
payload_desc: Padded upright case of sealed glass medication vials
motion_rationale: The fragile case limits the 1.8 m forward leg to 0.045 m/s, and the 0.24 m leftward handoff adjustment uses 0.02 m/s for 12 seconds.

title: Pump Delivery After Warehouse Fire
description: Carry a restrained drainage pump and hose bundle 16 m along a cleared, level lane to the recovery crew. The six-module body cruises forward at 0.16 m/s with the heavy load, turns clockwise 90 degrees over 15 seconds in a 1.4 m staging square, then advances another 3 m. The route has been released for entry after structural and atmosphere checks.
payload_desc: Compact drainage pump with coiled hose in a low transport frame
motion_rationale: The 19 m loaded route uses 0.16 m/s forward travel on damp concrete, and the heavy pump requires a controlled 90-degree clockwise turn at 6 deg/s over 15 seconds.

title: First Aid Kits Between Seats
description: Move a low crate of first aid kits 7 m down an immobilized train carriage to the responder at the far vestibule. The 0.4 m square body passes between seat ends only 0.48 m apart at 0.10 m/s. At a missing-seat bay, slide left 0.45 m over 15 seconds to clear the aisle for responders, keeping the same heading throughout.
payload_desc: Low secured crate of dressings, splints, and first aid packs
motion_rationale: The 7 m seat aisle limits forward speed to 0.10 m/s, and the 0.45 m leftward move into the handoff bay takes 15 seconds at 0.03 m/s.

title: Scrubber Cartridge Refuge Delivery
description: Carry a replacement air-scrubber cartridge from the refuge chamber storage wall to the service cradle, following a 4.2 m forward lane at 0.14 m/s. Approach the cradle along a marked 0.84 m front-left diagonal at 0.042 m/s, preserving the cartridge's heading to match its keyed tray. The crew completes the cartridge exchange after the body stops.
payload_desc: Replacement scrubber cartridge in a restrained service tray
motion_rationale: The 4.2 m clear lane supports 0.14 m/s forward travel, while the keyed cradle needs a 20-second, 0.84 m front-left approach at 0.042 m/s.

title: Optical Reference Through Cold Aisle
description: Carry a vibration-isolated optical reference beside three rack inspection stations spaced 2.4 m apart. Travel forward at 0.08 m/s between stations and slide right 0.12 m over 8 seconds at each one to place the reference beside the rack camera. Slide left by the same amount before continuing; keep the reference facing the racks throughout.
payload_desc: Fragile optical calibration reference on a vibration-isolated mount
motion_rationale: The fragile reference travels the 2.4 m station intervals at 0.08 m/s, with each 0.12 m lateral approach and withdrawal taking 8 seconds at 0.015 m/s.

title: Inverter Row Thermal Survey
description: Carry a thermal scanner and its battery along a 36 m indoor inverter row, pausing at six marked cabinets. Use 0.26 m/s on the clear straight sections to keep the survey within five minutes. Turn counter-clockwise 180 degrees in the 1.6 m end bay over 10 seconds, then return down the same lane.
payload_desc: Low-mounted thermal scanner and secured auxiliary battery
motion_rationale: The 72 m round trip needs near-full 0.26 m/s forward travel to leave time for six short scans within 300 seconds, with a 10-second half-turn at 18 deg/s.

title: Wing Panel Camera Positioning
description: Move a low inspection camera rig 5 m beneath a parked aircraft wing at 0.125 m/s. At the marked panel, slide left 0.18 m over 18 seconds and rotate clockwise 6 degrees over 12 seconds to align the camera with the fastener row. Hold for the image sequence, then reverse 0.5 m at 0.05 m/s before the technician approaches.

constraints: marked stop short of landing gear

payload_desc: Low camera rig with ring light and calibration target
motion_rationale: The clear 5 m approach peaks at 0.125 m/s with a slower reverse withdrawal, while the 0.18 m lateral correction and 6-degree yaw require 0.01 m/s and 0.5 deg/s respectively.

title: Engine Room Sideways Sensor Pass
description: Carry an acoustic inspection recorder through a level machinery gap 0.49 m wide. Orient the six-module block with its 0.4 m dimension across the gap and slide right along the 3.6 m passage at 0.06 m/s, keeping the sensors pointed toward the engine casing. Slide left along the same route after a 30-second recording stop; do not turn between the machines.
payload_desc: Restrained acoustic recorder and directional microphone array
motion_rationale: The fixed sensor heading requires sideways travel in both directions, with each 3.6 m machinery-gap leg taking about 60 seconds at 0.06 m/s.

title: Bearing Alcove Inspection Retreat
description: Carry a thermal camera into three blind bearing-service alcoves off a turbine hall aisle. Each alcove is 2.8 m deep and 0.36 m wide, so the pair enters lengthwise at 0.14 m/s and reverses out along its entry line at 0.07 m/s. Turn clockwise 90 degrees over 3 seconds only in the broad aisle when selecting the next alcove.
payload_desc: Thermal inspection camera and compact data logger
motion_rationale: Each 2.8 m alcove takes about 20 seconds to enter at 0.14 m/s and 40 seconds to reverse at 0.07 m/s, while open-aisle quarter-turns use 30 deg/s.

title: Pipe Joint Gauge Registration
description: Move a laser joint gauge on a straight three-module body 6 m through a level pipe gallery at 0.12 m/s. At each of two inspection marks, slide right 0.09 m over 15 seconds, hold for measurement, then slide left to the travel line. Keep the gauge parallel to the pipe; no rotation is needed.
payload_desc: Laser joint gauge with low rigid mounting rail
motion_rationale: The 6 m gallery leg permits 0.12 m/s forward travel, while registering each gauge position requires 15-second, 0.09 m sideways moves at 0.006 m/s.

title: Enclosed Bridge Walkway Joint Survey
description: Carry a joint camera along the level, enclosed maintenance walkway inside a bridge box girder. Travel forward 8 m at 0.20 m/s, slide left 0.3 m over 5 seconds around a bracket, and follow a 1.2 m front-right diagonal at 0.12 m/s to the viewing mark. Rotate counter-clockwise 90 degrees over 6 seconds for the image, then reverse 1 m at 0.10 m/s to clear the access hatch.
payload_desc: Compact joint inspection camera with battery and light
motion_rationale: The clear 8 m leg uses 0.20 m/s with a slower reverse exit, while the bracket offset, 1.2 m diagonal, and quarter-turn require 0.06 m/s, 0.12 m/s, and 15 deg/s respectively.

title: Nacelle Analyzer Battery Transfer
description: Carry a 19 kg vibration analyzer and battery pack 3 m from the nacelle service platform to the gearbox inspection position. The four-module body is already inside the stopped turbine and advances at 0.075 m/s through the level equipment lane. Slide right 0.4 m over 20 seconds into the inspection pocket without rotating the heavy pack.
payload_desc: Vibration analyzer and auxiliary battery pack in a low restrained frame
motion_rationale: The heavy pack takes about 40 seconds to traverse the 3 m equipment lane at 0.075 m/s, followed by a 20-second rightward positioning move at 0.02 m/s.

title: Cleanroom Reference Wafer Delivery
description: Carry a sealed reference-wafer case 4.8 m from the inspection cabinet to the metrology bay using a cleanroom-qualified pair. Travel forward at 0.06 m/s with gentle starts, then move along a 0.48 m front-right diagonal over 24 seconds to the receiving outline. Preserve the case heading and let the technician lift it from the deck.
payload_desc: Sealed padded case containing a fragile reference wafer
motion_rationale: The reference wafer limits the 4.8 m forward route to 0.06 m/s, and the 0.48 m diagonal registration takes 24 seconds at 0.02 m/s.

title: Column Crack Scanner Registration
description: Move a small crack-imaging camera 2.4 m to a column in an enclosed parking level at 0.12 m/s. Slide left 0.06 m over 12 seconds and turn counter-clockwise 4 degrees over 8 seconds to center an existing crack in the camera view. Hold for a 30-second exposure sequence while the parking bay remains closed.
payload_desc: Short crack-imaging camera stand and illumination unit
motion_rationale: The 2.4 m approach uses 0.12 m/s, while centering the crack requires a 12-second lateral correction at 0.005 m/s and an 8-second yaw correction at 0.5 deg/s.

title: Ward Supply Tote Orientation Circuit
description: Carry a latched supply tote on a straight three-module body between four ward collection points along a 24 m hospital route. Cruise forward at 0.24 m/s, stopping in marked 1 m turning squares to face the tote label toward staff. Make six alternating clockwise and counter-clockwise 90-degree turns, each over 2.5 seconds.
payload_desc: Latched tote of wrapped dressings and ward consumables
motion_rationale: The 24 m route uses 0.24 m/s between handoffs, while six 90-degree label-facing turns require 36 deg/s to complete each in 2.5 seconds.

title: Breakfast Tray Through Service Pinch
description: Carry two covered breakfast settings on a secured low tray 10.5 m down the hotel service corridor at 0.15 m/s. Pass through a 0.47 m gap beside a parked linen cart with the square body held straight. At the room-service alcove, slide right 0.35 m over 14 seconds for staff to collect the tray without blocking the corridor.
payload_desc: Secured tray with two covered breakfast settings and retained cups
motion_rationale: The loaded 10.5 m carpet route uses 0.15 m/s, while the narrow handoff alcove requires a 14-second, 0.35 m rightward slide at 0.025 m/s.

title: Exception Bag Conveyor Docking
description: Carry one tagged exception bag 12 m from the manual screening table toward a stopped transfer conveyor at 0.25 m/s. Follow the marked 2.16 m front-left diagonal approach at 0.24 m/s across the clear docking apron. Finish with a 0.15 m forward creep at 0.015 m/s so an attendant can transfer the bag.
payload_desc: Compact tagged suitcase held in a shallow retaining tray
motion_rationale: The 12 m transfer lane supports 0.25 m/s forward travel before a slower docking creep, and the clear 2.16 m diagonal apron crossing takes 9 seconds at 0.24 m/s.

title: Assembly Cell Kit Replenishment
description: Carry a 26 kg fastener kit 15 m down the line-side aisle at 0.25 m/s. Turn clockwise 90 degrees over 5 seconds in the cell apron, slide left 0.8 m at 0.08 m/s, then approach the receiving stand along a 0.6 m front-right diagonal at 0.04 m/s. After the operator removes the kit, reverse 1.2 m at 0.12 m/s to clear the stand.
payload_desc: Clamped divided kit tray containing fasteners and small assembly brackets
motion_rationale: The clear 15 m aisle permits 0.25 m/s with a slower reverse departure, while the 0.8 m slide, 0.6 m docking diagonal, and five-second quarter-turn use 0.08 m/s, 0.04 m/s, and 18 deg/s.

title: Rare Book Return to Conservation
description: Carry a returned rare volume in a fitted archival cradle from the secure return desk to the conservation room, 6.4 m away. Travel forward at 0.08 m/s with gradual starts and stops, keeping the cradle facing the same direction. Slide left 0.2 m over 20 seconds beside the receiving table for the conservator to lift the volume.
payload_desc: Fragile rare volume supported in a padded archival cradle
motion_rationale: The fragile volume limits the 6.4 m forward route to 0.08 m/s, and the 0.2 m table alignment takes 20 seconds at 0.01 m/s sideways.

title: Sample Rack Hatch Alignment
description: Carry a sealed secondary container of sample tubes 3.6 m from the preparation bench to the analyzer pass-through at 0.12 m/s. Slide right 0.048 m over 12 seconds to align the container with the hatch centerline, then creep forward the final 0.08 m at 0.008 m/s. Stop at the floor mark while the technician transfers the container through the hatch.
payload_desc: Sealed upright secondary container holding a rack of capped sample tubes
motion_rationale: The 3.6 m transfer leg peaks at 0.12 m/s before a 0.008 m/s final creep, while the 48 mm rightward hatch correction takes 12 seconds at 0.004 m/s.

title: Carton Restock Behind Rolling Racks
description: Carry a strapped carton of toiletries through a 0.46 m gap between fixed rolling racks to the shelf-filling station 5.4 m away. Advance the four-module square at 0.09 m/s without turning in the gap. At the widened station, slide left 0.42 m over 14 seconds; after unloading, slide right and reverse along the entry lane.
payload_desc: Strapped compact carton of boxed toiletries
motion_rationale: The 5.4 m rack lane takes about 60 seconds each way at 0.09 m/s, with 0.42 m lateral entry and exit moves taking 14 seconds each at 0.03 m/s.

title: Anchor Kit Into Partition Recess
description: Carry an anchor kit on a straight three-module body into a 4.5 m blind recess between newly installed indoor partitions. Advance at 0.15 m/s on the swept slab, stop for the installer to remove the kit, then reverse the full distance at 0.09 m/s because the 0.38 m passage has no turning space. The route ends before the unfinished threshold and contains no steps.
payload_desc: Lidded anchor and fixing kit secured in a narrow tray
motion_rationale: The 4.5 m recess takes about 30 seconds to enter at 0.15 m/s and 50 seconds to reverse out at 0.09 m/s, with no room for lateral moves or yaw.

title: Camera Dolly Blind Set Retreat
description: Carry a low camera head into a 3.2 m blind corridor built inside the studio set. Advance at 0.08 m/s to the start mark, then film while reversing the same 3.2 m at a steady 0.04 m/s. The 0.5 m scenic passage ends at a fixed wall, so retain the camera heading and make no sideways moves or turns.
payload_desc: Compact cinema camera head and battery on a low vibration-isolated mount
motion_rationale: The 3.2 m setup approach uses 0.08 m/s, while the filmed reverse retreat uses 0.04 m/s for an 80-second moving shot without changing camera heading.

title: Gallery Label Stand Placement
description: Carry a folded label stand and mounting supplies 11 m across the closed gallery at 0.22 m/s. Turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees over 4 seconds in the open center, then follow a 1.5 m rear-left diagonal at 0.10 m/s around a bench while keeping the tray facing the installer. Slide right 0.24 m over 12 seconds to the taped handoff outline beside the display plinth.
payload_desc: Folded label stand and a secured box of mounting supplies
motion_rationale: The 11 m gallery crossing uses 0.22 m/s, while the four-second quarter-turn, 15-second rear-left diagonal, and 12-second rightward alignment require 22.5 deg/s, 0.10 m/s, and 0.02 m/s.

title: Shoring Kit Through Cleared Corridor
description: Carry a 9.6 kg compact shoring kit to the search crew along a cleared, level strip through a collapsed office corridor. The two-module body travels lengthwise through a 0.32 m gap, covering the 8 m approach in about 70 seconds before reversing along the same route. At the delivery recess, slide left 0.18 m in roughly 7 seconds and slide right again after unloading.
payload_desc: Compact shoring kit secured in a low tray
motion_rationale: Forward and reverse travel peak at 0.12 m/s for the roughly 70-second corridor legs, while the short delivery-recess slides need only 0.028 m/s.

title: Office Smoke Survey Circuit
description: Carry a thermal camera and gas sampler around four cleared office junctions on a smoke-filled floor. Move forward between junctions along 3 m legs taking about 20 seconds, stopping on 1.1 m square clear areas to turn in place. Make two clockwise and two counter-clockwise 90-degree turns, allowing about 5 seconds for each turn and settling.
payload_desc: Thermal camera, gas sampler, and protected sensor mast
motion_rationale: The short office legs require 0.16 m/s forward peaks, and repeated 90-degree reorientations use 24 deg/s peaks to leave settling time within each five-second turn.

title: Garage Recess Search Passes
description: Carry a camera and listening sensor into three dead-end parking recesses on one level of a damaged garage. Each cleared recess is 5 m deep and only 0.34 m wide between debris boundaries, so enter forward in about 32 seconds and reverse out in about 43 seconds without turning. Slide right 0.9 m across the clear entrance apron between recesses, allowing about 12 seconds per transfer.
payload_desc: Low camera head and acoustic search sensor
motion_rationale: Forward entry peaks at 0.17 m/s with slower reverse exits, while the 0.9 m apron transfers need rightward sway peaks of 0.085 m/s.

title: Basement Pump Delivery
description: Carry a 19 kg portable pump and coiled discharge hose across a basement with a uniform 5 mm layer of water on a flat floor. Use a water-protected four-module square body to travel forward 10 m in about 100 seconds along a surveyed clear route. Slide right 0.6 m into the pump staging position over about 15 seconds, unload, then slide left and reverse to the starting area.
payload_desc: Portable pump and coiled hose restrained on the deck
motion_rationale: The wet-floor approach and reverse return use 0.105 m/s peaks, with 0.045 m/s lateral peaks for the fifteen-second pump-positioning slides.

title: Tunnel Sensor Relay Run
description: Carry a radio relay and crack camera 48 m into a level service tunnel after a quake. The inspected route is straight and clear, with a 0.6 m minimum passage between temporary supports; reach the survey mark in about 190 seconds. Pause for a camera sweep, then reverse the full distance without turning.
payload_desc: Radio relay pack and crack-inspection camera
motion_rationale: Forward and reverse peaks of 0.26 m/s support the approximately 190-second, 48 m straight legs with time for acceleration and stopping.

title: Evacuation Station Oxygen Delivery
description: Carry a secured 7.2 kg emergency oxygen kit from the corridor supply point to a staffed evacuation station. motion_rationale: The corridor legs use 0.195 m/s forward and reverse peaks, while 0.078 m/s diagonal peaks allow controlled twelve-second approaches and withdrawals at the receiving tray.

title: Landing Door Listening Check

The 0.31 m passage between stored equipment and the wall ends at the door, requiring a 2.4 m forward approach in about 30 seconds and a reverse exit. Remain on the landing throughout and do not turn near the stair opening.

motion_rationale: Aisle travel peaks at 0.09 m/s with a slower reverse alignment correction, and 0.015 m/s sway peaks support the twelve-second seat-gap slides.

After the technician removes the head, slide left and withdraw diagonally rear-right along the approach path.

motion_rationale: Gentle 0.085 m/s diagonal peaks fit the fifty-five-second underwing traverses, while 0.029 m/s sway peaks allow twelve-second fixture-alignment slides.

title: Engine Room Gauge Survey

motion_rationale: The short deck segments need 0.125 m/s forward peaks, and 17 deg/s yaw peaks allow seven-second quarter-turns with controlled starts and stops.

title: Turbine Hall Thermal Traverse

title: Nacelle Cabinet Side Scan

title: Garage Column Scanner Dock

Move diagonally front-left along a 6 m clear path to a marker in about 40 seconds, then continue along the same diagonal for the final 0.35 m to the scanner dock over about 10 seconds. motion_rationale: Forward travel peaks at 0.18 m/s with slower loaded reversing for the forty-two-second exit, and the apron quarter-turn uses a 25 deg/s clockwise peak.

constraints: firm bonded carpet without loose edges

payload_desc: Closed box of brackets, padded mounts, and hand tools
motion_rationale: The clear aisle permits 0.16 m/s forward travel, the 15-second diagonal needs a 0.13 m/s peak, the table approach uses 0.025 m/s rightward motion, and an 18 degrees/s clockwise peak fits the six-second turn.

title: Collect Tote from Long Aisle
description: Send a 2-by-3 body 24 m forward down a straight picking aisle to collect a 24 kg tote from a deck-height transfer shelf. Reverse along the same aisle after loading because there is no turning pocket, budgeting about 100 seconds for each travel leg.
payload_desc: Latched tote of packaged machine components
motion_rationale: A 0.25 m/s peak in both forward and reverse fits each 24 m leg into roughly 100 seconds while allowing end-of-aisle braking.

title: Shuttle Glassware on Mini Pallet
description: Carry a 7.5 kg foam-lined miniature pallet of glass vials across an 8 m cross-dock lane on two modules docked end to end. Travel forward in about 95 seconds, then slide left 0.25 m at no more than 0.018 m/s into a padded receiving cradle without rotating the load.
payload_desc: Deck-sized miniature pallet with foam-separated glass vials
motion_rationale: The fragile pallet needs a gentle 0.095 m/s forward peak for the 95-second crossing and a 0.018 m/s left slide into the receiving cradle.

title: Transfer Dense Fastener Tote
description: Move a 9.6 kg fastener tote on a two-module body from a shelf transfer plate to the packing station 6 m ahead. Allow about 45 seconds for the loaded run, then slide right 0.4 m in about 10 seconds to meet the station's side-loading guides.

constraints: dense load centered across both modules

payload_desc: Lidded tote of steel fasteners
motion_rationale: A 0.145 m/s forward peak accommodates the heavy tote's 45-second run, and a 0.045 m/s rightward peak completes the 0.4 m station transfer approach in about 10 seconds.

title: Scan Lower Rack Stock Labels
description: Carry a 4.8 kg low-mounted scanner, battery, and protective enclosure along 12 m of lower rack labels using one module. Move forward at no more than 0.085 m/s for readable images, pausing at each bay, then reverse 0.6 m at the final bay to rescan an obscured label.
payload_desc: Rack-label scanner with battery and protective enclosure
motion_rationale: Forward scanning and the short reverse rescan share a 0.085 m/s image-quality limit, leaving time within the job for bay stops under the near-capacity instrument load.

title: Receive Trailer Carton at Bay
description: Receive an 8 kg carton from a worker at the trailer mouth, with the two-module body staying entirely on the level loading-bay floor. Reverse 3 m clear of the unloading position in about 20 seconds, then travel 2.2 m diagonally rear-right in about 16 seconds to a receiving dock offset behind a bollard.

constraints: do not cross dock edge or bridge

payload_desc: Secured carton of boxed electrical fittings
motion_rationale: The 20-second reverse clearance needs a 0.165 m/s peak, and the offset receiving dock requires a rear-right diagonal peaking at 0.15 m/s over its 2.2 m approach.

title: Align Frozen Reagent Transfer Box
description: Carry a 16 kg closed reagent box on a square four-module body along 4 m of dry cold-storage aisle in about 50 seconds. At the transfer hatch, slide left 60 mm at 0.006 m/s and correct the heading clockwise by up to 4 degrees at 1 degree/s before staff take the box.
payload_desc: Latched insulated box of frozen reagent packs
motion_rationale: A 0.09 m/s forward peak fits the cold-room transit, while the hatch requires a 0.006 m/s left slide and a clockwise correction limited to 1 degree/s.

title: Feed Mezzanine Conveyor Parts Tray
description: Carry a 4.9 kg tray of machined parts 3.5 m forward along the flat mezzanine to a deck-height conveyor inlet using one module. Allow about 40 seconds for travel, then creep the last 0.15 m forward at 0.01 m/s into the locating stop while the conveyor is paused.
payload_desc: Retained tray of machined steel parts
motion_rationale: The near-capacity tray needs a 0.10 m/s forward transit peak for the 40-second run, followed by a slower 0.01 m/s final locating approach.

title: Dock Returned Electronics Bin
description: Carry a 6.5 kg returns bin on a two-module body through a 5 m straight lane in about 30 seconds. Keep its barcode facing the sorter and move 1.5 m diagonally front-right between two sorting carts in about 12 seconds to enter the marked receiving pocket.

constraints: sorting carts locked in marked positions

payload_desc: Lidded bin of returned handheld electronics
motion_rationale: A 0.18 m/s forward peak meets the 30-second lane transit, and a 0.14 m/s front-right diagonal peak fits the 12-second docking approach while preserving barcode orientation.

title: Retrieve Tray Between Mobile Racks
description: Enter a locked-open mobile-rack aisle with two modules docked end to end and move 4 m forward in about 55 seconds to receive a 7 kg tray. Slide left 30 mm at 0.005 m/s to meet the shelf guides, slide right to recenter after loading, and reverse out without turning.
payload_desc: Shallow tray of packaged spare parts
motion_rationale: Forward and reverse travel peak at 0.08 m/s in the narrow rack aisle, while 0.005 m/s slides provide the 30 mm shelf alignment and recentering.

title: Rush Prescription Packs to Checker
description: Carry a 1.8 kg sealed prescription tray on three modules arranged in a straight row down an 18 m reserved fulfilment lane in about 72 seconds. At the checker station, slide right 0.45 m in about 7 seconds while keeping the patient labels facing forward.
payload_desc: Sealed tray of labeled prescription packs
motion_rationale: The 72-second priority transit requires a near-full 0.265 m/s forward peak, followed by a 0.075 m/s rightward peak for the seven-second station approach.

title: Place Search Camera at Gap
description: Carry a 2.6 kg camera and light on two modules docked end to end along a cleared 3 m strip of collapsed corridor in about 50 seconds. Stop before the rubble, slide left 50 mm at 0.007 m/s, and turn counter-clockwise up to 8 degrees at 2 degrees/s to aim through a wall gap.
payload_desc: Low-mounted search camera and LED light
motion_rationale: The cleared corridor warrants a 0.07 m/s forward peak, and aiming through the gap requires a 0.007 m/s left slide plus a counter-clockwise turn limited to 2 degrees/s.

title: Search Smoke-Obscured Office Alcove
description: Take a 9 kg thermal-camera and air-monitor package on a 2-by-3 body 8 m forward into an office corridor ending at a locked records room. Pause to inspect door gaps, then reverse the same 8 m because the corridor offers no turning space, allowing about 90 seconds of movement in each direction.
payload_desc: Thermal camera, air monitor, and protected battery pack
motion_rationale: Forward entry and reverse withdrawal peak at 0.10 m/s to cover each 8 m leg in roughly 90 seconds while retaining stopping margin in smoke.

title: Deliver Radio Beside Garage Column
description: Carry a 4 kg radio and medical pouch on a two-module body along 5 m of swept parking-garage slab in about 45 seconds. Follow a cleared 1.6 m diagonal front-left lane between debris piles in about 20 seconds to a responder handoff mat beside a column.

constraints: no exposed reinforcement in wheel path

payload_desc: Protected radio and compact medical supply pouch
motion_rationale: A 0.125 m/s forward peak fits the swept-slab leg, while the debris-bounded handoff approach needs a slower 0.09 m/s front-left diagonal peak.

title: Survey Basement Water Entry Points
description: Carry a 5 kg inspection camera and water-level probe on three modules in an L shape through a basement with a flat floor and water no deeper than 5 mm. Move forward between four marked survey points at no more than 0.055 m/s, stopping in clear 1 m squares to turn in place clockwise and counter-clockwise through 90-degree views in about 7 seconds each.
payload_desc: Inspection camera and low-mounted water-level probe
motion_rationale: Wet-floor transit is limited to 0.055 m/s, and repeated 90-degree views use 15 degrees/s peaks in both yaw directions to complete each reorientation in about seven seconds.

title: Rush Sensor to Tunnel Team
description: Carry a 2 kg replacement gas sensor on a square four-module body along a surveyed, clear 30 m indoor service-tunnel section after a quake. Drive straight forward to the waiting inspection team in about 120 seconds, slowing only near the handoff point.
payload_desc: Padded replacement gas sensor kit
motion_rationale: The clear 30 m route and roughly 120-second delivery target require a 0.265 m/s forward peak with time reserved for acceleration and the final slowdown.

title: Slide Supplies Past Parked Beds
description: Carry a 22 kg evacuation-supply chest on a 2-by-3 body through a 0.48 m gap between parked beds, advancing 6 m in about 65 seconds without turning. In the wider nurse-station recess, slide left 0.7 m at no more than 0.035 m/s to place the chest beside the evacuation team.

constraints: body held square to narrow gap

payload_desc: Secured chest of evacuation blankets, masks, and dressings
motion_rationale: The tight bed gap limits the forward peak to 0.105 m/s for the 65-second passage, and the recess allows a controlled 0.035 m/s left slide.

title: Stage Breathing Kits on Landing
description: Carry an 18 kg chest of breathing masks on a 2-by-3 body through a flush doorway onto a 2.2 m square stairwell landing, moving forward 2 m in about 20 seconds. Inside the guarded staging area, turn clockwise 90 degrees in about 5 seconds, move diagonally front-right 0.6 m in about 9 seconds, then reverse 0.25 m slowly to the marked handoff line.

constraints: all motion inside marked staging area

payload_desc: Secured chest of breathing masks and filter cartridges
motion_rationale: Entry peaks at 0.115 m/s before a slower reverse alignment, the nine-second diagonal needs a 0.08 m/s peak, and a 24 degrees/s clockwise peak fits the five-second landing turn.

title: Recover Heat-Damaged Evidence Recorder
description: Carry a 3.6 kg heat-damaged recorder in a padded cradle from a cleared warehouse fire scene to an investigator's tray 4 m away. Move forward in about 65 seconds, then slide right 0.18 m at 0.009 m/s without turning so the cracked casing stays supported in the same orientation.

constraints: no loose soot piles in wheel path

payload_desc: Heat-damaged recorder secured in a padded evidence cradle
motion_rationale: The damaged recorder requires a gentle 0.07 m/s forward peak over the 65-second run and a 0.009 m/s right slide for the supported handoff.

title: Deliver First Aid Through Carriage
description: Carry a 14 kg first-aid box on a square four-module body 10 m forward through the 0.46 m seat aisle of a stationary train, allowing about 120 seconds. At the wider wheelchair bay, slide left 0.5 m at no more than 0.03 m/s to reach responders, then slide right back into the aisle and reverse to the vestibule after unloading.

constraints: sideways movement confined to wheelchair bay

payload_desc: Latched first-aid box with dressings and splints
motion_rationale: A 0.095 m/s forward and reverse peak preserves clearance along the seat aisle, while 0.03 m/s left and right slides serve the wheelchair-bay handoff and recentering.

title: Transfer Refuge Chamber Absorbent Pack
description: Carry a 15 kg replacement carbon-dioxide absorbent assembly in a padded tray on a square four-module body across 3 m of flat mine-refuge chamber floor in about 45 seconds. Turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees in about 12 seconds within the clear central bay, then slide right 0.35 m at 0.014 m/s to the technician without jolting the brittle cartridge housings.
payload_desc: Padded absorbent cartridge assembly with brittle sealed housings
motion_rationale: The fragile cartridges need a gentle 0.08 m/s forward peak, a 9 degrees/s counter-clockwise peak for the 12-second turn, and a 0.014 m/s right slide to the technician.

title: Deliver Glass Infusion Bottles
description: Carry a padded crate of glass infusion bottles from hospital stores to the ward supply alcove on a six-module 0.6 by 0.4 m body. Cruise forward along the 18 m corridor in 150 seconds, keeping the crate level over flush floor joints. At the alcove, slide left 0.45 m over 15 seconds without rotating; staff unload the bottles.
payload_desc: Secured crate of glass infusion bottles in foam dividers
motion_rationale: The fragile bottles require a 0.12 m/s forward cruise over 18 m and a gentle 0.03 m/s left slide for the 0.45 m alcove alignment.

title: Dock Breakfast Tray Carrier
description: Take a covered breakfast tray on a four-module square body from the service pantry to a room-service handoff pedestal. Travel forward along the 9 m carpeted corridor at a 75-second cruise pace, then approach the pedestal diagonally front-right across a 0.84 m path in 12 seconds. Keep the tray facing the guest-room doors throughout the approach.
payload_desc: Covered breakfast tray with two meals and sealed drinks
motion_rationale: The 9 m corridor cruise needs 0.12 m/s surge, while the 0.84 m front-right docking path takes 12 seconds at 0.07 m/s.

title: Return Misrouted Cabin Bag
description: Carry one small cabin bag from the baggage exception desk to a low receiving nest beside the reclaim conveyor. Cross a marked 13 m service lane forward at a 50-second cruise pace, then move diagonally front-left along a 1.2 m guide stripe in 10 seconds. The bag stays strapped lengthwise on the two-module body, and an attendant lifts it off at the nest.
payload_desc: Small cabin bag secured within the carrier footprint
motion_rationale: The clear 13 m lane supports 0.26 m/s forward travel, followed by a slower 0.12 m/s front-left approach over the 1.2 m docking stripe.

title: Exchange Assembly Fixture Kits
description: Deliver a tray of assembly fixtures into a 4.8 m blind line-side pocket using a four-module square body. Enter forward at a 40-second cruise pace, wait while the operator exchanges trays, then reverse out at the same pace because the pocket has no turning bay. Once clear, slide right 0.6 m in 10 seconds into the marked return lane.
payload_desc: Low tray of steel assembly fixtures
motion_rationale: Both 4.8 m pocket traversals use 0.12 m/s surge, and the 0.6 m right slide takes 10 seconds at 0.06 m/s.

title: Move Dense Book Returns
description: Carry a compact bin of returned reference books from the library intake hatch to the sorting desk. The two-module body travels forward along a 7.2 m shelving aisle at a 60-second cruise pace, then turns clockwise through 90 degrees in six seconds inside a clear junction. Slide left 0.36 m in six seconds to put the heavy bin within the librarian's reach.
payload_desc: Compact bin of heavy reference books
motion_rationale: The loaded aisle cruise requires 0.12 m/s surge, the desk offset requires 0.06 m/s left sway, and the six-second quarter-turn requires 15 deg/s clockwise yaw.

title: Transfer Sealed Assay Samples
description: Move a secured sample cooler from laboratory accession to the analyzer handoff shelf on a four-module square body. Cruise forward along the 6 m aisle in 40 seconds, turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees in five seconds at the junction, and follow a 0.72 m front-right diagonal into the handoff bay in nine seconds. Slide left 0.16 m in eight seconds for shelf alignment, then reverse 1.2 m in 12 seconds after staff remove the cooler.
payload_desc: Latched insulated cooler containing sealed assay tubes
motion_rationale: Forward cruising peaks at 0.15 m/s with reverse limited to 0.10 m/s, while the timed diagonal, shelf slide, and quarter-turn require 0.08 m/s, 0.02 m/s, and 18 deg/s respectively.

title: Restock Blind Stockroom Bay
description: Take a carton of shampoo refills into a 3.6 m dead-end bay behind the retail stock shelves. The two modules are docked lengthwise so their 0.2 m width fits the narrow passage; enter forward at a 30-second cruise pace. After the stock clerk unloads the carton, reverse the entire 3.6 m at a 40-second cruise pace without turning or sliding sideways.
payload_desc: Narrow carton of sealed shampoo refill pouches
motion_rationale: The loaded 3.6 m entry requires 0.12 m/s forward surge, while the blind reverse exit is slower at 0.09 m/s.

title: Rush Survey Targets Indoors
description: Carry a light case of laser survey targets across a swept indoor construction slab to the layout crew. Use a 24.3 m straight lane with a 90-second forward cruise, then take a 2.4 m front-left diagonal across the open staging square in 10 seconds. Stop at the crew's marked collection point without rotating the body.
payload_desc: Latched case of lightweight laser survey targets
motion_rationale: The long clear lane requires the full 0.27 m/s forward cruise, and the 2.4 m staging diagonal requires 0.24 m/s for its ten-second traverse.

title: Repeat Straight Camera Passes
description: Carry a compact remote camera on a low mount along an 8.4 m studio tracking lane. Make the forward filming pass at a 70-second cruise pace, then reverse along the same line at a 35-second cruise pace to reset for another take. Keep the body heading fixed and all cables off the floor.
payload_desc: Compact camera, battery, and low vibration-isolated mount
motion_rationale: The filming pass uses 0.12 m/s forward surge and the faster 8.4 m reverse reset establishes the 0.24 m/s surge peak.

title: Relocate Bronze Display Base
description: Move a small bronze display base in a padded cradle from the museum preparation bench to a gallery plinth after closing. A single module carries the dense load forward over a 4.5 m route at a 50-second cruise pace. Slide right 0.24 m in 12 seconds between the plinth feet so the conservator can lift the base straight up.
payload_desc: Small bronze display base secured in a padded cradle
motion_rationale: The near-capacity load travels forward at 0.09 m/s over 4.5 m, with a 0.02 m/s right slide for the close plinth alignment.

title: Collect Dense Fastener Bin
description: Send one module into a narrow picking aisle to collect a compact bin of steel fasteners from a low handoff shelf. Travel forward 6.6 m at a 60-second cruise pace, then slide left 0.12 m in six seconds beneath the handoff mark. After the picker loads the bin, slide right to the aisle center and reverse out along the same route.
payload_desc: Compact lidded bin of steel fasteners
motion_rationale: The 6.6 m entry and reverse return use 0.11 m/s surge, while each 0.12 m shelf offset takes six seconds at 0.02 m/s.

title: Shuttle Sample Mini Pallet
description: Carry a 0.18 m square sample mini pallet holding a boxed valve across the cross-dock on one module. Cruise forward along the 10.4 m marked lane in 40 seconds, then follow a 1.05 m front-right diagonal into a floor-level receiving nest in 15 seconds. A worker removes the mini pallet; no full-size freight pallet is involved.
payload_desc: Small boxed valve on a secured sample mini pallet
motion_rationale: The 10.4 m cross-dock cruise needs 0.26 m/s forward surge, while the receiving nest requires a slower 0.07 m/s front-right diagonal.

title: Thread Tote Through Guide Rails
description: Carry a narrow electronics tote from a shelf handoff to a packing station on one module. Advance 3.2 m through a straight guide-rail passage at a 40-second cruise pace, with only 35 mm clearance on each side of the body. At the wider station mouth, slide left 0.18 m in 15 seconds to align the tote with the pickup marks without yawing.
payload_desc: Narrow lidded tote of packaged electronic components
motion_rationale: The tight 3.2 m passage limits surge to 0.08 m/s, and the 0.18 m station offset takes 15 seconds at 0.012 m/s left sway.

title: Scan Alternating Rack Faces
description: Carry a short barcode camera mast on a four-module square body through six inventory scan stations spaced 2.4 m apart. Cruise forward between stations at 0.16 m/s, covering each interval in 15 seconds. At each station, turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees in two seconds to scan the left rack, turn clockwise 180 degrees in four seconds to scan the right rack, then turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees to face down the aisle again.
payload_desc: Barcode camera, short mast, and auxiliary battery
motion_rationale: The 2.4 m station spacing requires 0.16 m/s surge for each 15-second interval, and the repeated timed rack-facing turns require 45 deg/s yaw in both directions.

title: Receive Trailer Inspection Cases
description: Use three modules docked lengthwise to carry an inspection-equipment case from a trailer's rear receiving position to the bay table. The trailer is immobilized with its floor level to a secured flush bridge plate; advance 2.1 m across this route at a 30-second cruise pace. At the table, slide right 0.09 m in nine seconds, then creep forward the final 0.12 m in 12 seconds to meet the transfer marks.
payload_desc: Narrow latched inspection-equipment case
motion_rationale: The level trailer route allows 0.07 m/s surge, reduced to 0.01 m/s for final contact-free alignment, with the 0.09 m right adjustment also using 0.01 m/s.

title: Run Chilled Reagent Shuttle
description: Carry a small insulated reagent box from the cold-room entrance to the far-end handoff shelf on one module. The straight 21.6 m aisle is dry and clear, allowing a 90-second forward cruise. After a technician exchanges the box, reverse down the same aisle at the same pace because the shelf end has no turning space.
payload_desc: Compact insulated box of sealed chilled reagents
motion_rationale: Each uninterrupted 21.6 m aisle leg takes 90 seconds at a 0.24 m/s surge cruise, with reverse replacing a turn at the shelf.

title: Feed Mezzanine Conveyor Nest
description: Carry a narrow carton tray from the mezzanine packing bench to a low conveyor loading nest using three modules in a lengthwise row. Remain on the same mezzanine level and cruise forward along the 5.4 m guarded aisle in 30 seconds. Approach the nest diagonally front-left over a 0.9 m guide path in 15 seconds, keeping the long body parallel to the conveyor.
payload_desc: Narrow tray of small sealed shipping cartons
motion_rationale: The guarded 5.4 m aisle supports 0.18 m/s surge, and the parallel conveyor approach requires a 0.06 m/s front-left diagonal over 0.9 m.

title: Collect Returned Handset Trays
description: Collect a tray of returned handsets from a test-bench nest on a three-module lengthwise body. Starting in the central sorting lane, move diagonally rear-right along a 1.32 m marked approach in 12 seconds so the tray's pickup edge stays facing the technician. After loading, retrace the path diagonally front-left, then travel forward 4.2 m to the sorting table at a 30-second cruise pace.
payload_desc: Partitioned tray of returned mobile handsets
motion_rationale: The reciprocal 1.32 m diagonal paths require 0.11 m/s in rear-right and front-left directions, followed by 0.14 m/s surge over the 4.2 m sorting lane.

title: Dock Within Mobile Racking
description: Take a narrow archive-parts tray down the temporarily opened aisle of a mobile-racking system on three modules docked lengthwise. With rack motion interlocked off, cruise forward 7 m in 50 seconds to the widened end pocket. Move diagonally front-right along a 0.48 m path in 12 seconds to the floor-level pickup nest, then withdraw diagonally rear-left and reverse out after unloading.

constraints: diagonal movement only in end pocket

payload_desc: Narrow archive tray of boxed replacement parts
motion_rationale: The 7 m aisle legs use 0.14 m/s surge, while each 0.48 m diagonal docking or withdrawal takes 12 seconds at 0.04 m/s.

title: Align Prescription Cassette Carrier
description: Carry a sealed prescription cassette on two modules docked side by side, forming a body 0.4 m wide and 0.2 m long. Travel forward 2.8 m through the 0.46 m pharmacy-cell passage at a 35-second cruise pace. In the wider handoff pocket, slide right 0.14 m in 14 seconds to align the cassette label with the fixed reader, then slide left before reversing out.
payload_desc: Sealed low-profile prescription cassette
motion_rationale: The closely bounded 2.8 m passage requires 0.08 m/s surge, and the reader alignment and return each use 0.01 m/s sway over 0.14 m.

title: Probe Cleared Corridor Slot
description: Send a low thermal camera and microphone into a structurally cleared corridor segment beside fallen ceiling panels, using three modules in a lengthwise row. Advance 3 m along the swept, flat 0.32 m slot at a 50-second cruise pace without climbing debris. At a wider opening, slide left 0.12 m in 12 seconds to look through a doorway gap, slide right to recenter, then reverse out.

constraints: loose debris removed from wheel path

payload_desc: Low-mounted thermal camera, microphone, and radio
motion_rationale: The confined 3 m search slot limits surge to 0.06 m/s, while the doorway observation offset requires 0.01 m/s sway in both directions.

title: Dock Smoke Survey Relay
description: Carry a thermal survey head and radio relay on a six-module 0.6 by 0.4 m body to a marked observation dock inside a smoke-filled office floor. Follow the mapped 10.8 m cleared corridor forward at a 90-second cruise pace, then turn clockwise 90 degrees in three seconds in the open reception area. Approach the wall dock diagonally front-left over 1.2 m in 20 seconds so the relay antenna keeps its planned orientation.
payload_desc: Thermal survey head, radio relay, and secured battery pack
motion_rationale: The smoke survey route uses 0.12 m/s surge, the six-module body makes its three-second quarter-turn at 30 deg/s, and the wall dock requires a 0.06 m/s front-left approach.

title: Search Garage Debris Recess
description: Carry a camera and acoustic sensor into a blind recess between debris piles on a parking garage's level slab. The two-module lengthwise body advances 5.4 m along a swept channel at a 60-second cruise pace and pauses to listen near the blocked end. Reverse the full distance at a 90-second cruise pace because the channel offers no turning space; do not cross rubble or use the garage ramps.
payload_desc: Low camera, acoustic sensor, and protective housing
motion_rationale: The 5.4 m entry needs 0.09 m/s forward surge, while the slower blind retreat uses 0.06 m/s reverse surge.

title: Recover Fragile Water Samples
description: Carry a foam rack of sealed glass water-sample vials from a basement sampling point to the dry recovery station on three modules docked lengthwise. Use splash-protected modules on a surveyed flat route with no more than 3 mm of standing water, cruising forward 4.8 m in 80 seconds. At the dry station, slide right 0.24 m in 12 seconds to present the rack for lifting without turning or jolting the vials.
payload_desc: Secured foam rack of sealed glass water-sample vials
motion_rationale: The wet 4.8 m route and fragile vials require 0.06 m/s forward surge, followed by a gentle 0.02 m/s right slide at the dry recovery station.

title: Survey Level Tunnel Reach
description: Carry a low lidar, gas monitor, and lighting battery on a six-module 0.6 by 0.4 m body through a cleared service-tunnel reach after a quake. Cruise forward along the straight 48 m level floor in 200 seconds, stopping at four marked points for readings. At the surveyed 1.5 m turning bay, turn counter-clockwise 180 degrees in six seconds and drive forward back to the entry at the same cruise pace.
payload_desc: Low lidar, gas monitor, lights, and secured instrument battery
motion_rationale: Each 48 m tunnel traverse uses a 0.24 m/s forward cruise between stops, and the six-module body completes its end-bay half-turn at 30 deg/s.

title: Frozen Ingredient Tote Transfer
description: Carry a 14.4 kg insulated ingredient tote on three modules docked in a line from a freezer pick face to the packing vestibule. Drive forward along the 12 m clear aisle in a 60 s steady travel segment, then slide right 0.3 m over 10 s to line up with the unloading shelf. Keep the long body facing down the aisle throughout.
payload_desc: Sealed tote of frozen ingredient packs
motion_rationale: The loaded aisle segment needs 0.2 m/s forward for 12 m in 60 s, followed by a controlled right slide at 0.03 m/s for 0.3 m in 10 s.

title: Four Station Conveyor Feed
description: Move a 7 kg carton tray between four conveyor induction stations on a guarded, level mezzanine using a 2x2 body. Each station is 2.4 m from the next, with a 15 s steady forward leg and a 90-degree clockwise turn in place over 3 s at each marked turning pad. Operators transfer cartons only after the body stops.
payload_desc: Retained tray of small shipping cartons
motion_rationale: Successive 2.4 m forward legs take 15 s at 0.16 m/s, while repeated 90-degree clockwise reorientations require 30 deg/s during their 3 s turning intervals.

title: Returns Tray Scale Placement
description: Bring a 6.2 kg returns tray on a three-module line into the marked bay beside a bench scale. Advance 1.8 m in a 30 s steady segment, slide left 0.12 m over 12 s, and turn counter-clockwise 4 degrees over 4 s to match the scale guide. After staff remove the tray, reverse 1.8 m along the same approach.
payload_desc: Tray of individually bagged returned electronics
motion_rationale: The 1.8 m approach and retreat use 0.06 m/s over 30 s each, with a 0.01 m/s left correction and 1 deg/s counter-clockwise trim matching the stated alignment intervals.

title: Dense Rack Battery Delivery
description: Carry a secured 9.6 kg replacement battery cassette on a fore-aft pair through an opened mobile-rack aisle. Travel forward 7.2 m in a 60 s steady segment, then slide left 0.18 m over 9 s into the marked handoff position without changing heading. Reverse out after the cassette is removed.
payload_desc: Clamped replacement battery cassette
motion_rationale: Forward delivery and reverse withdrawal need 0.12 m/s for the 7.2 m aisle segments, while the 0.18 m left handoff offset takes 9 s at 0.02 m/s.

title: Urgent Pharmacy Tote Shuttle
description: Carry a 1.3 kg lidded prescription tote on a 2x2 body from the dispensing cell to the checking bench. The reserved straight lane includes a 13 m steady transit segment that must take 50 s, followed by a right slide of 0.24 m over 8 s into the bench bay. Keep the tote facing the checker throughout.
payload_desc: Lidded tote of packaged prescriptions
motion_rationale: The timed 13 m straight segment requires 0.26 m/s forward, and the final 0.24 m right slide requires 0.03 m/s over 8 s.

title: Corridor Void Camera Delivery
description: Take a 1.8 kg camera and two-way speaker on a fore-aft pair down a cleared strip of intact corridor floor to inspect a gap beneath a fallen partition. Advance 4.2 m over a 70 s steady segment, then slide right 0.08 m over 8 s through a 0.25 m-wide offset throat opening into a wider observation pocket. Slide left again and reverse out after the search team reviews the view.
payload_desc: Low-profile camera and two-way speaker assembly
motion_rationale: The cleared 4.2 m corridor legs use 0.06 m/s, and the narrow offset throat requires 0.01 m/s lateral movements for each 0.08 m correction over 8 s.

title: Office Doorway Thermal Check
description: Position a 3.2 kg thermal camera and air sampler on a 2x2 body outside a smoke-filled office doorway. Follow the cleared 3 m corridor segment forward in 50 s, slide left 0.15 m over 15 s to center the sensor view, and turn clockwise 6 degrees over 6 s to aim through the door opening. Hold for the incident operator's reading before reversing along the approach.
payload_desc: Thermal camera and sealed air-sampling instrument
motion_rationale: Forward and reverse corridor travel use 0.06 m/s for 3 m in 50 s, with a 0.01 m/s left slide and 1 deg/s clockwise aim adjustment for precise doorway alignment.

title: Garage Shoring Tool Handoff
description: Deliver an 11 kg case of shoring wedges on a 2x2 body across a swept, level section of parking garage to the rescue crew. Travel forward 5.6 m in a 40 s steady segment, then slide left 0.6 m over 20 s between two fixed debris piles through a 0.46 m-wide cross passage. Slide right back through the passage and reverse to staging after unloading.
payload_desc: Secured case of shoring wedges and hand tools
motion_rationale: The 5.6 m approach and retreat use 0.14 m/s, while the tight 0.6 m cross passage requires left and right slides at 0.03 m/s over 20 s each.

title: Basement Water Level Check
description: Send one splash-protected module carrying a 0.7 kg camera and water-depth probe along the flat basement service strip. In a verified 3 mm film of water, move forward 2.4 m in a 60 s steady segment and slide right 0.06 m over 6 s to sight a gauge through a 0.24 m-wide gap between a pipe guard and a cabinet. Slide left to recenter and reverse out after the reading.
payload_desc: Sealed camera and shallow-water depth probe
motion_rationale: Wet-floor travel is limited to 0.04 m/s for each 2.4 m leg over 60 s, and the gauge alignment uses 0.01 m/s lateral corrections of 0.06 m over 6 s.

title: Tunnel Joint Camera Alignment
description: Carry a 2.6 kg illuminated crack camera on a fore-aft pair along the intact, level tunnel maintenance strip to a marked lining joint. Drive forward through a 6.3 m steady segment in 70 s, slide left 0.09 m over 9 s, and turn counter-clockwise 3 degrees over 6 s to align the camera with the joint. Reverse along the strip after recording.
payload_desc: Illuminated crack camera with onboard recorder
motion_rationale: The 6.3 m transit legs require 0.09 m/s, while joint alignment needs a 0.01 m/s left slide and a 0.5 deg/s counter-clockwise correction over the specified intervals.

title: Evacuation Supply Cart Docking
description: Bring a secured 23 kg load of blankets and sealed respiratory supply packs on a 2x3 body to a staffed evacuation transfer point. Advance along the 8.4 m clear corridor segment in 70 s, then slide right 0.2 m over 20 s and turn clockwise 5 degrees over 5 s inside the broad transfer alcove. Stop with the deck aligned beside the supply cart for manual unloading.
payload_desc: Blankets and sealed respiratory supply packs
motion_rationale: Corridor transit needs 0.12 m/s for 8.4 m in 70 s, followed by a 0.01 m/s right slide and 1 deg/s clockwise trim to align the loaded deck with the cart.

title: Extended Landing Supply Run
description: Move an 18 kg case of rescue lighting batteries on a 2x3 body along the unusually long, flat transfer landing between two enclosed stair cores. The route stays entirely on the same level and includes an 18.2 m straight segment covered forward in 70 s, with slow stopping at the crew's marked unload point. Reverse along the same straight route after unloading; no part of the job enters either stair flight.
payload_desc: Case of rescue lighting battery packs
motion_rationale: The long unobstructed landing requires 0.26 m/s forward and reverse to cover each 18.2 m steady travel segment in 70 s.

title: Fire Recovery Sensor Docking
description: Carry a 12 kg sealed atmosphere-monitoring case on a 2x3 body from the recovery staging line to a sampling dock on a cooled warehouse floor. Drive forward 5.1 m in a 30 s steady segment, then approach the dock diagonally front-left for 1.2 m along the diagonal path over 20 s to pass a fixed hose reel. After sampling, withdraw diagonally rear-right along the same path and reverse to staging.
payload_desc: Sealed atmosphere-monitoring case with sampling inlet
motion_rationale: The straight staging legs use 0.17 m/s for 5.1 m in 30 s, and the angled dock approach and withdrawal use a diagonal path speed of 0.06 m/s for 1.2 m in 20 s.

title: Carriage Seat Row Search
description: Take a 0.9 kg camera and speaker on one module through a stationary, level train carriage to check beneath a seat row. Drive forward 4.8 m in a 40 s steady segment, slide left 0.24 m over 8 s into the seat bay, and turn clockwise 90 degrees over 6 s in the clear bay center. Move diagonally front-right 0.3 m over 6 s to obtain the view, then retrace that diagonal, undo the turn, slide right, and reverse down the aisle.
payload_desc: Compact camera and two-way speaker
motion_rationale: The job needs 0.12 m/s aisle travel, 0.03 m/s lateral seat-bay entry, 15 deg/s quarter turns, and 0.05 m/s diagonal viewing moves, each retraced at the same speed.

title: Refuge Chamber Supply Shuttle
description: Deliver a 17 kg box of drinking-water pouches and breathing-mask cartridges on a 2x2 body along a refuge chamber's level service annex. The straight outbound route includes a 22.5 m steady segment scheduled for 90 s before the staffed handoff point. Reverse along the same lane after unloading because the terminal bay has no turning space.
payload_desc: Water pouches and sealed breathing-mask cartridges
motion_rationale: Both long straight legs require 0.25 m/s to cover their 22.5 m steady segments in 90 s, with reverse travel avoiding a turn in the terminal bay.

title: Cold Aisle Thermal Survey
description: Carry a 4.8 kg thermal and airflow instrument on a 2x3 body down a data-centre cold aisle. Drive forward 10.8 m in a 60 s steady segment, slide left 0.18 m over 9 s at a rack face and right again, then move diagonally front-right 0.8 m over 8 s through the open end bay. Turn counter-clockwise 180 degrees over 6 s on the marked 1.2 m-square pad before driving forward into the adjacent aisle.
payload_desc: Thermal camera and low-profile airflow measurement rig
motion_rationale: The survey needs 0.18 m/s straight travel, 0.02 m/s rack-offset slides, a 0.1 m/s diagonal end-bay crossing, and a 30 deg/s half turn to meet the specified segment times.

title: Inverter Room Thermal Sprint
description: Move a 1.6 kg thermal recorder on a 2x3 body between two inverter banks inside a level equipment room. Cross the clear floor diagonally front-left along a 10.4 m path in a 40 s steady segment to capture the second bank during the same operating interval. Finish with a right slide of 0.15 m over 5 s to center on its marked observation position.
payload_desc: Compact thermal recorder on a low mount
motion_rationale: The synchronized inspection requires a diagonal path speed of 0.26 m/s for 10.4 m in 40 s and a final 0.03 m/s right slide for 0.15 m in 5 s.

title: Underwing Panel Camera Pass
description: Carry a 2.4 kg upward-facing panel camera on a 2x2 body beneath a parked aircraft wing. Advance 3.6 m in a 30 s steady segment, then slide right 1.2 m over 40 s through a 0.45 m-wide corridor between padded maintenance fixtures while keeping the camera square to the panel seam. Slide left back through the corridor and reverse to the inspection station.
payload_desc: Upward-facing camera and diffuse inspection light
motion_rationale: The approach and retreat need 0.12 m/s for 3.6 m in 30 s, while the fixture corridor requires 0.03 m/s sideways passes of 1.2 m over 40 s.

title: Engine Room Analyzer Positioning
description: Carry an 18.8 kg vibration analyzer and contact-probe kit on a 2x2 body across a dry, level engine-room deck while the ship is alongside. Travel forward 4.4 m in a 40 s steady segment and turn clockwise 90 degrees over 10 s in the clear service bay. Slide left 0.24 m over 12 s beside the machinery guard so a technician can attach the probe leads.
payload_desc: Vibration analyzer, contact probes, and protected lead reel
motion_rationale: The heavy instrument travels at 0.11 m/s for the 4.4 m approach, turns at 9 deg/s for a controlled 10 s quarter turn, and slides left at 0.02 m/s into probe-access position.

title: Turbine Hall Reading Shuttle
description: Carry a 1.2 kg dosimeter and thermal logger on a 2x2 body between two marked turbine-hall observation points. The reserved straight lane has a 16.2 m steady segment that must be covered forward in 60 s during the scheduled reading window. Pause at the second point, then reverse over the same segment to the collection station.
payload_desc: Dosimeter and thermal data logger
motion_rationale: The reading window requires near-full straight speed of 0.27 m/s to cover each 16.2 m steady segment in 60 s, outward forward and homeward in reverse.

title: Pipe Gallery Acoustic Circuit
description: Carry a 1.7 kg acoustic leak recorder on a 2x2 body along the flat pipe-gallery service lane. Travel forward through a 12.5 m steady segment in 50 s, turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees over 2.5 s in the widened end bay, and continue forward along the branch to the second recording mark. The recorder takes readings only while stopped.
payload_desc: Acoustic leak recorder with isolated microphone mount
motion_rationale: The 12.5 m timed transit needs 0.25 m/s forward, and the widened branch junction permits a 36 deg/s counter-clockwise quarter turn over 2.5 s.

title: Bridge Bearing Walkway Survey
description: Carry a 3.4 kg bearing-inspection camera on a 2x2 body along an enclosed, level maintenance walkway beneath the bridge deck. Enter each dead-end bearing pocket forward, using an 8.4 m steady segment over 60 s on the longest pocket, then slide right 0.1 m over 10 s for the image and left again. Reverse the full pocket length because its 0.52 m width does not permit the body to turn.
payload_desc: Side-looking bearing camera and inspection light
motion_rationale: The longest pocket needs 0.14 m/s forward and reverse for 8.4 m in 60 s each, with 0.01 m/s lateral image offsets of 0.1 m over 10 s.

title: Nacelle Oil Analyzer Delivery
description: Move a 14.2 kg portable oil analyzer on three modules docked fore-aft from the nacelle's flat lift receiving pad to the gearbox sampling station. With the turbine parked, advance 2.7 m along the level service strip in a 45 s steady segment, then slide right 0.12 m over 12 s into the sampling position. After the technician finishes and removes the analyzer, slide left and reverse to the receiving pad.
payload_desc: Compact portable oil analyzer with retained sample bottles
motion_rationale: The heavy analyzer moves at 0.06 m/s along each 2.7 m service-strip leg and uses 0.01 m/s lateral shifts of 0.12 m over 12 s for sampling access.

title: Cleanroom Reference Plate Transfer
description: Carry a 3.6 kg sealed optical reference-plate cassette on a fore-aft pair from its cleanroom storage stand to the inspection tool's loading mark. Use gentle acceleration into a 2.4 m forward segment covered in 60 s, then slide left 0.08 m over 16 s and turn clockwise 2 degrees over 8 s to align the cassette handle with the tool guide. A technician lifts the cassette after the body settles.
payload_desc: Sealed cassette containing a fragile optical reference plate
motion_rationale: The fragile cassette requires 0.04 m/s forward travel for 2.4 m in 60 s, a 0.005 m/s left alignment slide, and a 0.25 deg/s clockwise trim to match the loading mark gently.

title: Parking Column Base Scan
description: Position a 1.1 kg close-range scanner on one module at three marked views around a parking-structure column base. Approach forward through a 1.5 m steady segment in 30 s, slide left 0.12 m over 12 s to center the first target, and turn counter-clockwise 30 degrees over 10 s for the second view. Move diagonally rear-right 0.18 m over 12 s to the third mark, stopping fully for each scan.
payload_desc: Close-range concrete surface scanner
motion_rationale: The scan sequence needs 0.05 m/s forward approach, 0.01 m/s left centering, 3 deg/s counter-clockwise reorientation, and a 0.015 m/s rear-right diagonal move to meet the marked viewing intervals.

title: Align Evacuation Supply Tray
description: Carry a 7 kg tray of evacuation masks along a cleared hospital corridor to a supply receiver beside a fire door. The two-module body travels forward along 6 m at a 50-second cruise pace, then slides left 0.24 m over 12 seconds to align the tray within 10 mm of the receiver. After staff remove the tray, reverse through the same corridor.
payload_desc: Secured tray of evacuation masks and straps
motion_rationale: Forward and reverse cruise at 0.12 m/s along the 6 m corridor, while the 0.24 m left slide over 12 seconds limits alignment speed to 0.02 m/s.

title: Rush Landing Radio Batteries
description: Move a 3 kg battery case between two rescue staging tables on one flat stairwell landing, with the four modules docked as a 0.4 m square. The screened route has a 5.2 m straight section requiring a 20-second cruise, followed by a clockwise 90-degree turn in three seconds inside a marked turning square. Drive forward along the final short leg to the receiving table.
payload_desc: Latched case of charged handheld-radio batteries
motion_rationale: The urgent 5.2 m straight cruise requires 0.26 m/s forward, and the three-second clockwise quarter-turn requires 30 deg/s.

title: Distribute Fire Assessment Sensors
description: Carry a 9 kg sensor case through a warehouse bay released for entry after the fire, using three modules in a straight row. Advance along cleared 3.2 m lanes at a 20-second cruise pace, stopping in 0.9 m turning pockets to turn in place toward each marked delivery position. The route alternates clockwise and counter-clockwise 90-degree turns, each taking four seconds.
payload_desc: Secured case containing portable atmosphere sensors
motion_rationale: Cleared 3.2 m lanes support 0.16 m/s forward cruise, while repeated four-second quarter-turns require 22.5 deg/s in both yaw directions.

title: Dock Carriage Medical Supplies
description: Deliver a 12 kg medical pack through a stationary train carriage on a level track, using a four-module square body. Travel forward down the 7.2 m cleared aisle at a 40-second cruise pace, then approach the responder's receiver diagonally front-right along a 0.84 m path over 12 seconds. Reverse straight out after unloading, keeping the body orientation fixed throughout.
payload_desc: Strapped medical pack with dressings and airway supplies
motion_rationale: The aisle needs forward and reverse cruise up to 0.18 m/s, and the 0.84 m front-right docking path over 12 seconds requires 0.07 m/s diagonally.

title: Retrieve Refuge Air Monitor
description: Retrieve an unattended 4 kg air-monitor case from a dead-end equipment recess inside a mine refuge chamber. The two-module body enters forward along a 2.8 m lane at a 20-second cruise pace, then reverses along that lane after an attendant secures the case. At the open end it slides right 0.48 m over eight seconds to reach the collection table without turning.
payload_desc: Portable air monitor in a secured protective case
motion_rationale: The dead-end lane requires forward and reverse cruise at 0.14 m/s, followed by a 0.48 m right slide over eight seconds at 0.06 m/s.

title: Dock Cold Aisle Scanner
description: Carry a 6 kg airflow scanner on three modules arranged in a straight row down a data-centre cold aisle. Cruise forward along 9.6 m in 60 seconds, then move diagonally front-left along a 0.72 m path over 12 seconds into an offset calibration dock in the end cross-aisle. Leave the dock diagonally rear-right along the same path before reversing down the aisle.
payload_desc: Low-mounted airflow scanner and calibration interface
motion_rationale: Aisle travel uses 0.16 m/s forward and reverse cruise, while both directions of the 0.72 m diagonal docking path take 12 seconds at 0.06 m/s.

title: Position Inverter Thermal Recorder
description: Move a 5 kg thermal recorder between an inverter-room storage shelf and a floor calibration dock. Drive forward along a 4.5 m clear lane at a 30-second cruise pace, then follow a 0.9 m front-right diagonal over ten seconds to enter the dock between cabinet plinths. Keep the two-module body parallel to the cabinets throughout the approach.
payload_desc: Thermal recorder with rigid low-height mounting cradle
motion_rationale: The 4.5 m lane sets forward cruise at 0.15 m/s, and the ten-second 0.9 m diagonal approach requires 0.09 m/s without yaw.

title: Carry Underwing Inspection Rig
description: Carry a 28 kg inspection rig beneath a parked aircraft wing on a six-module 0.6 by 0.4 m body. Cruise forward along a 12 m marked lane in 80 seconds, then slide left 1.2 m over 20 seconds to place the upward-facing sensor beneath the access panel. After the scan, slide right along the same path and reverse out without turning beneath the wing.
payload_desc: Secured upward-facing inspection rig including cradle and battery
motion_rationale: The loaded 12 m lane uses 0.15 m/s forward and reverse cruise, while 1.2 m lateral positioning legs over 20 seconds require 0.06 m/s in either sway direction.

title: Shuttle Engine Room Recorder
description: Shuttle a 2 kg vibration recorder across a ship's engine room while the vessel is secured alongside, using a two-module body. The cleared deck route requires forward cruise along 10.4 m in 40 seconds, followed by a right slide of 0.6 m over five seconds into a technician's receiving bay. Slide left to leave the bay and reverse along the same route after the recorder is read.
payload_desc: Vibration recorder in a small latched case
motion_rationale: The 10.4 m transit cruise needs 0.26 m/s in forward and reverse, while five-second 0.6 m bay transfers require 0.12 m/s sideways.

title: Traverse Turbine Instrument Gap
description: Carry an 8 kg acoustic inspection package on a four-module square body through a 0.48 m gap between turbine-hall instrument bases. Enter the gap forward, then slide right along its 1.8 m transverse section over 30 seconds while preserving the package's orientation. Slide left back through that section and reverse along the 3.6 m entry lane at a 30-second cruise pace.
payload_desc: Low-profile acoustic inspection package
motion_rationale: Entry and withdrawal cruise at 0.12 m/s along 3.6 m, while the tightly bounded 1.8 m lateral passage takes 30 seconds at 0.06 m/s in each direction.

title: Survey Long Pipe Gallery
description: Carry a 23 kg recording package along a straight indoor pipe gallery on a six-module rectangular body. Cruise forward along the 52 m survey section in 200 seconds, stopping at marked positions for upward images. At the clear end bay, turn in place clockwise through 180 degrees over eight seconds and drive forward back to the entry.
payload_desc: Centered camera, recorder and battery assembly
motion_rationale: The 52 m survey cruise requires 0.26 m/s forward, and the six-module body's eight-second clockwise half-turn requires 22.5 deg/s.

title: Align Bearing Inspection Camera
description: Position a 10 kg upward-looking camera on an enclosed, level maintenance walkway beneath a bridge deck. The four-module square body cruises forward along 4.8 m in 40 seconds, then slides left 0.18 m over 12 seconds and turns counter-clockwise six degrees over four seconds to frame a bearing label. After imaging, undo the small turn, slide right and reverse to the access room.
payload_desc: Upward-looking camera assembly and protected battery
motion_rationale: The access cruise uses 0.12 m/s in surge, while the 12-second 0.18 m slides and four-second six-degree corrections require 0.015 m/s sway and 1.5 deg/s yaw.

title: Align Nacelle Borescope Station
description: Move a 7 kg borescope station across the level service floor inside a locked-out wind-turbine nacelle, using a four-module square body. Advance 1.8 m at a 30-second cruise pace, then slide right 0.16 m over eight seconds to match a gearbox inspection stand. Reverse 0.12 m over six seconds for final stand clearance, preserving orientation throughout.
payload_desc: Borescope controller and coiled probe in a secured cradle
motion_rationale: Forward cruise peaks at 0.06 m/s over the 1.8 m approach, with slower 0.02 m/s reverse clearance and a 0.02 m/s right slide for precise stand alignment.

title: Deliver Cleanroom Metrology Standard
description: Transport a 29 kg metrology standard in a sealed cradle across a semiconductor cleanroom bay on a six-module body. Cruise forward along the 8.4 m service lane in 60 seconds, then move diagonally front-left along a 1.12 m path over 16 seconds into the inspection station. After the measurement, withdraw diagonally rear-right and reverse along the lane.
payload_desc: Metrology standard including sealed transport cradle
motion_rationale: The heavy standard travels at 0.14 m/s on the 8.4 m straight legs and 0.07 m/s on each 16-second diagonal docking leg.

title: Scan Parking Column Row
description: Carry a 4 kg column-imaging package along a closed, level parking-structure aisle. The two-module body cruises forward along 48 m in 200 seconds, pausing at six columns and sliding left 0.6 m over six seconds at each scan position. Slide right after each scan and reverse the full aisle to return; the route excludes vehicle ramps.
payload_desc: Side-facing imaging package with battery
motion_rationale: The long 48 m legs need 0.24 m/s forward and reverse cruise, while six-second 0.6 m column offsets require 0.1 m/s lateral motion.

title: Restock Hospital Dressing Store
description: Carry 26 kg of dressing packs in latched bins from central stores to a ward supply room on a six-module body. Follow a 65 m straight service corridor at a 250-second cruise pace, then turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees over five seconds inside the supply-room turning bay. Drive forward to the receiving mark for staff unloading.
payload_desc: Latched bins of sterile dressing packs
motion_rationale: The 65 m corridor requires 0.26 m/s forward cruise, and the loaded body's five-second counter-clockwise quarter-turn requires 18 deg/s.

title: Deliver Hotel Breakfast Boxes
description: Carry 6 kg of closed breakfast boxes from the service pantry to three staffed collection points off a hotel corridor. The two-module body cruises forward along 6.6 m corridor sections in 30 seconds and turns in place toward each collection point inside widened alcoves. Alternate clockwise and counter-clockwise 90-degree turns over three seconds each to face staff and then resume the route.
payload_desc: Closed breakfast boxes in a secured retaining tray
motion_rationale: Corridor sections use 0.22 m/s forward cruise, and repeated three-second quarter-turns toward and away from collection points need 30 deg/s in both yaw directions.

title: Rush Baggage Routing Labels
description: Move a 2.5 kg box of replacement routing labels between two desks inside the airport baggage hall's segregated service area. Three modules in a straight row cruise forward along 13.5 m in 50 seconds, then take a 2.08 m front-left diagonal across a clear square in eight seconds. Keep the box facing the receiving desk and finish with a slow straight approach.
payload_desc: Closed box of replacement baggage-routing labels
motion_rationale: The urgent 13.5 m straight cruise requires 0.27 m/s, and the eight-second 2.08 m front-left crossing needs 0.26 m/s diagonally.

title: Present Assembly Fastener Kits
description: Carry an 8 kg partitioned fastener tray to four line-side stations on a two-module body. Cruise forward along 3.6 m links at an 18-second pace, turning in place clockwise or counter-clockwise through 90 degrees over 2.5 seconds to present the tray's labeled edge at each station. At the last station, reverse 0.45 m over five seconds before turning back toward the return lane.
payload_desc: Latched partitioned tray of assembly fasteners
motion_rationale: Forward links peak at 0.2 m/s with a slower 0.09 m/s reverse clearance, while 2.5-second quarter-turns require 36 deg/s in both directions.

title: Return Fragile Folio Volumes
description: Move 14 kg of fragile returned folio volumes in padded horizontal boxes from the library returns desk to the conservation bench on a four-module square body. Cruise forward along a 9.6 m staff aisle in 80 seconds, then slide left 0.42 m over 14 seconds beside the bench. Reverse along the aisle after unloading, using gentle starts and stops to protect brittle bindings.
payload_desc: Padded boxes containing fragile folio volumes
motion_rationale: The padded volumes travel at 0.12 m/s forward and reverse cruise, with the 0.42 m bench alignment spread over 14 seconds at 0.03 m/s sideways.

title: Transfer Sealed Laboratory Samples
description: Carry a 6 kg sealed sample carrier from the preparation bench to the analyzer room on a two-module body. Cruise forward along 5.4 m in 30 seconds, turn counter-clockwise 90 degrees over six seconds, and slide right 0.36 m over six seconds through an offset doorway. Approach the receiving stand diagonally front-left along 0.64 m over eight seconds, then reverse 0.3 m over five seconds after unloading.
payload_desc: Sealed sample carrier with restrained tube racks
motion_rationale: The route peaks at 0.18 m/s forward with a 0.06 m/s reverse clearance, while the timed doorway slide, diagonal approach and quarter-turn require 0.06 m/s sway, 0.08 m/s diagonal and 15 deg/s yaw.

title: Restock Narrow Backroom Shelf
description: Carry 17 kg of boxed toiletries on a four-module square body to a retail backroom shelf through a 0.46 m passage between fixed rack ends. Cruise forward along the 4.2 m approach in 35 seconds, then slide left 1.2 m over 24 seconds through the narrow transverse passage without turning. Slide right to withdraw and reverse to the receiving area after staff unload the boxes.
payload_desc: Restrained stack of boxed toiletries
motion_rationale: The approach and return use 0.12 m/s surge, while the 1.2 m transverse passage takes 24 seconds at 0.05 m/s in either lateral direction.

title: Rush Interior Layout Markers
description: Deliver a 2 kg case of layout markers across a cleared indoor construction slab between two survey crews. The two-module body cruises forward along 10.8 m in 40 seconds, then crosses an open marked zone diagonally front-right along a 3.12 m path in 12 seconds. Stop at the receiving mat for hand collection; the route stays on one finished, level slab.
payload_desc: Latched case of layout markers and chalk refills
motion_rationale: The 10.8 m straight cruise requires 0.27 m/s forward, and the 3.12 m front-right crossing over 12 seconds requires 0.26 m/s diagonally.

title: Reposition Low Camera Dolly
description: Carry a 7.5 kg low-mounted camera package between three marked dolly positions on a film-studio floor. Travel forward along 2.4 m links at a 20-second cruise pace, then turn in place clockwise or counter-clockwise through 45 degrees over five seconds to face each set. At the final mark, slide left 0.54 m over nine seconds for the framing correction, with the camera secured against overturning.

constraints: camera package includes low mounting plate

payload_desc: Compact camera, battery and low mounting plate
motion_rationale: The 2.4 m links require 0.12 m/s forward cruise, five-second 45-degree reorientations need 9 deg/s yaw, and the nine-second 0.54 m framing slide needs 0.06 m/s sway.

title: Move Gallery Display Ballast
description: Carry a 9.5 kg display ballast cassette from the museum preparation room to a floor-mounted display base after closing. The two-module body cruises forward along a 7.7 m gallery route in 70 seconds, then slides right 0.28 m over eight seconds to align the cassette with the staff transfer cradle. After staff lift it off, slide left and reverse to the preparation room without turning near the exhibits.
payload_desc: Dense display ballast cassette including retaining cradle
motion_rationale: The near-capacity load uses 0.11 m/s forward and reverse cruise over 7.7 m, with eight-second 0.28 m lateral transfers limited to 0.035 m/s.

title: Deliver Corridor Evacuation Supplies
